parts.text: Outline one cause of impulse control disorders or non-substance addictive disorder.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the study by Grant et al. (2008) on the biochemical treatment of addiction to
gambling.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two weaknesses of the study by Grant et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the characteristics, types and measures of anxiety disorders.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate the characteristics, types and measures of anxiety disorders, including a discussion
of case studies. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain what is meant by the ‘disrupt-then-reframe’ sales technique investigated by Kardes
et al. (2007).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe how consumers would make purchase decisions according to the ‘theory of planned
behaviour’ (Ajzen, 1991).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain two practical applications of the theory of planned behaviour that would help a
company to sell products.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about environmental influences on consumers
(cognitive maps of retail locations, crowding in retail environments, shopper movement
patterns).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about environmental influences on consumers
(cognitive maps of retail locations, crowding in retail environments, shopper movement
patterns), including a discussion about reliability. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline how Fox et al. (1987) used a token economy in worksites to promote health.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe the procedure of the ‘whole-school’ Food Dude programme from the study by
Tapper et al. (2003).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the study by Tapper et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have discovered about misusing health services.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about misusing health services, including a
discussion about practical applications. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by ‘job satisfaction’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the quality of working life (QWL) questionnaire (Walton, 1974).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Discuss the use of self-reports to measure job satisfaction.

parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about traditional and modern theories of
leadership.
